title: Tiny argv parser: --name=value, short-option bundles with attached values, and -- end-of-options

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 1: a long option may be written --name=VALUE.
Rule 1: the value may be empty (--output= sets "").
Rule 1: the value is everything after the first = and may contain further = (--output=a=b sets "a=b").
Rule 1: the value is everything after the first = (verbatim).
Rule 1 applies to every long value option, including ones without a short name.
Rule 1: --flag=anything (including --flag=) raises UsageError.
Rule 1: the name is the text between -- and the first =; if unknown, UsageError.
Rule 2: -vn is equivalent to -v -n.
Rule 2: -oout.tar sets output to "out.tar".
Rule 2: -voout.tar sets verbose and output="out.tar".
Rule 2: the rest of the bundle after a value option is its value (-ov sets output="v", does not set verbose).
Rule 2: if the value letter is the last character, the next argument is its value (-vo out.tar).
Rule 2 (next argument is its value) + preserved behavior: the next argument is taken even if it begins with -.
Rule 2: if there is no next argument, UsageError.
Rule 2: any character processed as an option that is not a registered short option (-vz, -v-) raises UsageError.
Rule 2: the rest of the bundle after a value-taking letter is its value, not options.
Rule 3: -- is dropped and every following argument is a positional verbatim.
Rule 3: only the first -- is special; a later -- is a positional.
Rule 3: -- itself is dropped.
Rule 3: an argument consumed as an option value is not an end-of-options marker (--output -- -v).
Rule 4: repeatable options collect values from every spelling in command-line order.
Rule 4: for a non-repeatable option the last occurrence wins whatever its spelling.
Current behavior (preserved): every parse call starts from fresh defaults.
Current behavior (preserved): --name VALUE, -s VALUE, flags, interleaved positionals.
Current behavior (preserved): --output -v sets output to "-v".
Current behavior (preserved): a lone - is a positional argument.
Current behavior (preserved): a value option at the very end of argv raises UsageError.
Current behavior (preserved): unknown options raise UsageError.
Current behavior (preserved): flags default False, repeatable default [], value options default to their default.
